Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j

bench/seat_variants.py: recorded rollout decisions played again with the simulated seats set other ways

On the same layouts (drawn once a decision), every candidate on every layout: the plain draw as played, the top card,
a sharpened draw, a cut on unlikely cards, and the two sides set differently. Scored by the values' error against the
table's result for the card that was played (level, squared error, Brier) and by the cards chosen (double dummy on the
deal as it lay, hindsight). Rows are kept so the report can be reprinted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j

bench/value_check.py: the rollouts' values against the table's result; they are optimistic for the side deciding

For every recorded rollout decision: declarer's tricks the rollouts expected with the card played, and the contract's
chance, against the table's result; by role, stage and how clear the choice was; a calibration table. Read-only, numpy
only. On the gate's records (R3 blind against BEN, 2,039 deals): declaring +0.07, defending -0.18, the lead -0.15 tricks;
the same in self-play and with every round's net; larger for clear choices than close ones. The morning's oracle-layout
result (half of the early double-dummy loss remains when the layouts are the deal) is recorded with it.

scope: Stu collection versus testing allocation on named Azure hosts, Stu4c twins, rollout calibration/seat-variant replay, and sidplay auction-aware analysis.
disposition: Continue owned Gen8 collecting under the current frozen identity and approved mix. Stu continues Gen8 self-play on Azure1/3 and adopts Stu4c twins on Azure2/6; its BEN gate ends at650 on a resource/training decision, not an owned gate or completion. Calibration and seat variants are research; its kept-layout audit bug is in the replay bench only. PR33 and new board notice deploy auction-aware post-hand analysis to the public play server only. No local source/model/settings/corpus/worker/guard change, training, BEN, promotion, self-play opening or peer command.

play/: the analysis reads the auction (Sid's hand-fit scorer + the cell game)

Max, 14 Nov 09:08 PST: 'The engines should read the auction.' At the person's decisions with 8 cards or fewer, the
auction weight that ONE line provably wins (cells: East's suit lengths and the holders of up to two honour runs), for
the best card and the card played; as a defender, declarer's figure after each alternative. Floors only (proven lower
bounds). Exchanges in the 'why' are those the auction allows, with where the auction put the deciding card.
cells.cpp, celllib.py and pipeline.py vendored from research/conditional-claims-20261113. R4c bids deterministically
(argmax; no randomisation), so Sid's calls are read as precisely as its scorer fits them.
